sheets.title: Lower base and first terrace
sheets.prompt:
Create a highly detailed architectural SKETCH SHEET, landscape, on clean warm ivory paper, fine ink contour with rose/ivory watercolor materials and meticulous gold ornament. This is an extraction-and-extension study of the ORIGINAL PALACE shown in the one attached reference, not a new palace design. Three named structural assemblies on each sheet, with generous separation. Each assembly has a large clear front-three-quarter view, a smaller matching front elevation and a small true overhead footprint outline. All three views must depict the same object with identical bay counts, projections and attachments. A narrow top strip shows how these three parts join left-to-right in the original front, with upper/lower neighboring architecture only in faint gray context. Do not shrink the source's great windows into repetitive little doors. Preserve unequal west/east structure. Closed glazed wall apertures have actual recessed blue/lilac/pink glass and thick carved masonry; actual galleries are open. Carved spandrels, engaged lotus piers, gold leaf ribs, rose/starlight medallions, fine pierced parapets and veined pink and ivory stone must follow the reference. Canonical small fittings are installed for identity, not reinvented. Do not create a featureless box or a row of separated towers. Connected ranges have curved, chamfered and recessed fronts. All parts fully framed, even lighting. Print the title and the exact three component IDs and short names legibly beside parts. Label FRONT and REAR in each footprint. Mark new rear strip with restrained violet dashed line and 'PROPOSED REAR +30 GRID m'. Back extension goes only away from the locked front face, maintaining width and height, with continuous side return and roof. Rear strip is a proposed modelling allowance, not measured from illustration. It must not move the original gate, stair, cascade, front tower or window positions. Do not invent new crowns, bridges or ornament motifs. The sheet is a concept reference pending comparison, not an exact measured construction drawing. Detailed realistic palace architecture sketch, not icon art, not generic fantasy asset blocks.
TITLE: PAL-LAYER-01 — Lower base and first terrace.
Focus only on this level and the three requested source assemblies, not another complete castle.
PAL-LAYER-01-W Western lower glazed arcade and rounded projecting terrace: Extract the lower left curved continuous wall below the great windows. Preserve the three-lancet glazed rhythms, thick lotus pilasters, inward/receding returns and the small forward star-panel tower socket. Keep the western terminal tower as gray context beyond the seam; do not replace this range by a freestanding open colonnade.
PAL-LAYER-01-C Central paired dry stairs and wet cascade apron: Extract the original blue tiered central cascade, its central wet bed, original top landing, dry stair on EACH side, carved newels and lowest retaining cheeks. Both dry stairs and the central water cascade belong to this ONE connector assembly. Show the wet and dry routes distinctly; do not replace this by a single stair or circular fountain. Rear addition starts behind the landing, not in front of stairs.
PAL-LAYER-01-E Eastern lower nested arcade and angled return: Extract the lower right curved wall and unequal nested returning fronts, lower garden terrace, short side stair and star-panel projection. Preserve different east/west rhythm; do not mirror the western part. Show seats for original terminal tower and the higher projecting belvedere in gray context.
Print a small note: SOURCE GEN-37 / REAR DEPTH PROPOSED / PENDING REVIEW. The confirmed vertical body band is 0–60 grid m; tower crowns and attached projections may cross bands. Do not label visible source image bands as measured level cuts.

sheets.title: Gate wall and four great-window ranges
sheets.prompt: Make one very detailed fine-ink and watercolor architectural sketch sheet from this precise ORIGINAL FRONT CROP. Title PAL-LAYER-02 — Gate wall and four great windows. The crop is the authoritative view of this exact gate wall, not merely a style reference. Follow it faithfully. Top half: ONE big front elevation of the complete cropped wall, exactly TWO huge blue/pink/lilac pointed window bays to the left of ONE giant central gold glass gate and TWO huge pointed window bays to the right. Preserve the actual narrow shaft piers, gold floral tracery, gabled central rose-star medallion and source window envelope. The WEST GREAT WINDOW PAIR has small engaged pointed pier/pinnacle attachments, NOT large onion-domed corner towers. The large west pavilion and east domed belvedere belong beyond/behind this cropped wall, NOT new identical corner towers for each segment. Do not insert a freestanding domed tower at any join. Do not multiply the narrow pointed piers into tower masses. Subdivide the elevation only by two thin vertical dotted lines around the gate. Below it, print labels PAL-LAYER-02-W Western great-window pair, PAL-LAYER-02-C Ceremonial gate wall, PAL-LAYER-02-E Eastern great-window pair, with each label below its matching original section. Lower half: THREE corresponding isolated shallow overhead three-quarter studies, one per these exact sections. Wall fronts in the lower studies repeat exactly the top view and its bay count, thick rose and ivory marble walls, real recessed glazed apertures with matching source glass, intricately carved gold lotus pilasters and rose/star spandrels. Side returns extend backward modestly. At the rear only, show a light violet outline strip labeled PROPOSED REAR +30 GRID m. Keep front and width unchanged. Segment C has a rear-going roof hall behind the actual gate, while W and E have garden roofs with source railing and flowerbeds. Show existing central dry stairs and wet cascade only lightly below the original gate as context, do not redesign them. Plain warm ivory paper, sophisticated classical architectural sketch sheet, sharp fine detail, material swatches tiny at margin: rose marble, ivory marble, gold, indigo/lilac glass. Print SOURCE GEN-37 / REAR DEPTH PROPOSED / PENDING REVIEW. No decorative border towers, no copied symmetric end towers, no extra domes, no extra windows. Hidden rear geometry is a proposed study, not an exact source measurement.
